title: Conclusive Identification Via Noisy Classical Channel: Superactivation and Quantum Advantage
summary: We introduce conclusive identification task for classical channels: a receiver identifies transmitted inputs without error when possible, and responds inconclusively when outputs are ambiguous. For a symmetric not-fully-corrupted channel $N : X \to X$, the single-shot conclusive identification index $\mathrm{ci}_\circ(N)$ counts the maximum number of conclusively identifiable inputs.
